# r10n

> Routine automation in a native, accessible terminal application.

r10n provides contacts, PDF personalization, image optimization, website image
downloads, logo downloads, email, CSS conversion, file renaming, CSV validation,
and Markdown-to-PDF conversion. A Go/Charm frontend provides searchable task
selection, validated prompts, review, cancellation, and progress. Python runs
the automation worker through a versioned JSON Lines protocol.

## Install

The recommended installation is the checksum-verified standalone bundle:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pruthivithejan/r10n/main/install.sh | sh
r10n
```

The installer supports Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64. Windows x86_64 users can
download the standalone executable from GitHub Releases. A standalone bundle
does not require Python or uv at runtime.

Run a released version with uvx:

```bash
uvx --from git+https://github.com/pruthivithejan/r10n.git r10n
```

## Preferences and profiles

```bash
r10n setup
r10n config path
r10n configure --template /path/to/template.pdf
r10n config add-smtp-profile work
```

Settings and named profiles are stored in the OS per-user configuration
directory. SMTP passwords use the OS credential manager, not the JSON settings
file. No project-local config tree or `.env` discovery is used. `r10n --accessible`
selects linear prompts; `r10n --no-motion` disables animated progress.

## Automations

```bash
r10n contacts --input /path/to/numbers.txt --output /path/to/contacts.vcf --yes
r10n fill-pdfs --config conference --recipients /path/to/data.csv --yes
r10n images --input /path/to/photos --output /path/to/optimized --yes
r10n email --smtp-profile work --recipients /path/to/people.csv --body /path/to/message.txt --yes
r10n list --json
```

Headless execution needs complete inputs and `--yes`. The flag skips
confirmation, not validation. See [automation guides](automations/index.md) for
parameters and formats.

## Architecture and development

Go packages: `cmd/r10n`, `internal/cli`, `internal/tui`, `internal/backend`,
`internal/settings`, `internal/brand`. Python packages:
`src/r10n_backend/{__main__.py,registry.py,worker.py,settings.py,secrets.py,automations/}`.
The native package launcher and standalone binary use the same backend contract.

Developer-only checks from a source checkout:

```bash
./setup.sh test
./setup.sh check
./setup.sh build
```

`pyproject.toml` is the human-edited package version; use
`uv run --locked python scripts/release_version.py --check` to verify generated
release metadata.
